content:
Apple TV's current lineup is strong, led by hits like "Slow Horses," "Ted Lasso," "Dark Matter," and Matthew McConaughey's new comedy "Brothers." But there's even more on the way. Here's everything new coming to Apple TV in October.

The Last First: Winter K2

  • Date: October 2
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Documentary

"The Last First: Winter K2," directed by Amir Bar-Lev, tells a complex, thrilling, and moving story that exposes the extreme mountaineering industry and its ever-evolving culture. The film focuses on a 2021 expedition in which Icelander John Snorri Sigurjónsson and the Pakistani father-and-son duo Ali and Sajid Sadpara set out to summit K2 in winter, when conditions on the mountain are at their most brutal. The group soon finds themselves sharing this treacherous journey with influencer climbers and their photography crews, commercial expedition clients, and Nepali legend Nims and his team of Sherpas. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes viewers to K2's frozen peaks, where they face unpredictable weather and uncover an unexpected, layered story—one of strategy and determination, class and hierarchy, money and power—all unfolding in a life-or-death environment.

The Sisters Grimm (Season 2)

  • Date: October 2
  • Type: TV Series
  • Category: Kids & Family

Two orphaned sisters navigate a town full of fairy tale and fantastical characters, dealing with heroes and villains while investigating the mystery of their missing parents. "The Sisters Grimm" blends exploration, fantasy, and adventure to deliver important lessons for viewers of all ages.

Small Prophets

  • Date: October 7
  • Type: TV Series
  • Category: Comedy

"Small Prophets" tells the comedic story of eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley). Ever since his beloved Clea disappeared seven years ago, he's been living a remarkably ordinary life. He works at a hardware store, visits his father Brian (Sir Michael Palin), and holds out hope that Clea will return. One day, Brian shares an ancient recipe involving rainwater, horse manure, and a good deal of alchemy. Michael takes the recipe (skeptically) and sets out to create "homunculi"—magical sprites that can predict the future—hoping they'll answer his most burning question: "Can I see Clea again?"

Matchbox The Movie

  • Date: October 9
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Action

"Matchbox The Movie," adapted from the iconic Mattel toy, is an action-packed, globe-trotting adventure about a group of lifelong friends whose lives are turned upside down when CIA undercover agent Sean (John Cena)—their long-absent former leader—returns to their small town, unknowingly dragging them into a wild, world-saving international chase.

Tenzing

  • Date: October 16
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Drama

"Tenzing" is based on a true story and recounts the lesser-known tale of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok). A gifted Himalayan mountaineer, Tenzing teamed up with New Zealand climber Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston) to become one of the first people to summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo), Tenzing gained the support of expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe). Together, they persuaded Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) to make Tenzing an official member of the British climbing team rather than relegating him to logistics support. Where Western climbers saw "Everest" as a summit to conquer, Tenzing revered "Chomolungma" as a sacred mother goddess. The resulting ascent is charged with tension born of differing backgrounds, classes, and ambitions, while also brimming with the dangers inherent to high altitude. But at the top of the world, empires, status, and ambition all fall away, leaving two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust—and for Tenzing, fulfilling a lifelong dream while answering a spiritual calling.

Where's Wanda? (Season 2)

  • Date: October 21
  • Type: TV Series
  • Category: Dark Comedy

Apple's first German-language series, "Where's Wanda?" is a dark comedy about Dedo and Carlotta Klatt, a couple desperate to find their 17-year-old daughter Wanda, who's been missing for months with police no closer to solving the case. The family decides to investigate on their own, with the help of their tech-savvy younger son Ole, who procures surveillance equipment. Posing as utility company workers, they plant listening devices throughout the neighborhood—eventually covering half the community—and discover that their neighbors are nothing like they appear behind closed doors.

Nocturne

  • Date: October 30
  • Type: TV Series
  • Category: Crime Drama

The series tells the story of Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber), a former soldier turned homicide detective who's grown weary of the gritty streets of Philadelphia and moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania for a quieter life. But when the town and his family come under threat from a cunning serial killer named Jurek Walter (Graham), Jonah must protect everything he holds dear. When the urgent hunt for Jurek's final victim forces Jonah to send the woman he regards as a daughter, FBI agent Saga Bauer (Beetz), to confront Jurek alone, just how far will Jonah go?

New Episodes: "Slow Horses," "Brothers," and More

Apple TV also has new episodes dropping in October for several currently airing series, including:

  • "Ted Lasso": Jason Sudeikis-led comedy, airing through October 7
  • "Last Seen": crime thriller, airing through October 7
  • "Slow Horses": acclaimed British spy series, airing through October 21
  • "Dark Matter": Joel Edgerton-led sci-fi series, airing through October 30
  • "Brothers": comedy co-starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, airing through November 4

Which new Apple TV release are you planning to watch in October? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV costs $14.99 per month, or you can bundle it via an Apple One subscription.
